declaration.negotiation_history_statement:
Hargrove Lane LLP, court-appointed interim class counsel, submits this statement in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). The settlement resulted from successive proposals and counterproposals addressing both class relief and attorneys’ fees. Fees were discussed from the initial proposal, not deferred until after agreement on class relief. The proposed fee amount decreased during negotiations and remained unchanged during the final exchanges over the class fund. Accordingly, counsel does not represent that the monetary negotiations were wholly separate.

The binding settlement provides a $26 million class fund and an additional $3.25 million for attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to independent court approval. There is no clear-sailing provision. Any fees not awarded will augment the class fund rather than revert to Brightline. All plaintiffs’ counsel fees and expenses, including any court-approved allocation among counsel, must come from that fee pool, not additional deductions from class relief.

Only documented, court-approved notice and administration expenses, capped at $750,000, may reduce the class fund. At least $25.25 million is therefore reserved for class payments, with unused administration funds and unawarded fees benefiting the class. There is no reversion of class funds or allowance for unspecified deductions. Brightline will separately bear its internal implementation costs.

Distribution will be automatic, without claim forms or continued or renewed membership requirements. Payments must deliver actual monetary value, with automatic fallback payments where card credits cannot be completed. Counsel will obtain itemized vendor bids to establish a workable distribution plan. The administration cap is contractual, not an established vendor estimate, and cannot justify inadequate notice or omission of identified recipients. Distribution feasibility and the proposed notice program remain matters for substantiation in the approval process.

Counsel believes the settlement is fair, reasonable, and adequate in light of the substantial automatic monetary recovery, unresolved certification risk, uncertainty of prevailing at trial, and an anticipated two-to-three-year delay before trial. The $26 million gross class fund represents approximately 40.6% of the $64 million in disputed renewal charges; the minimum $25.25 million available for payments represents approximately 39.5%. These figures describe aggregate recovery, not a promised individual recovery percentage.

Counsel recognizes that its contingent financial interest and the existence of overlapping actions warrant scrutiny. This request rests on the benefits and protections secured for the class, not counsel’s interest in compensation or securing approval before competing actions. Concurrent negotiation of fees and relief should be considered candidly, alongside the absence of clear sailing, independent fee review, and allocation of unawarded fees to the class. Counsel requests preliminary approval and authorization of an appropriate notice process, subject to the Court’s assessment of the proposed allocation, release, distribution plan, adequacy of representation, and other Rule 23(e) requirements. Final approval and any fee award remain for the Court after notice and an opportunity for class members to be heard.
